provenance.scope: Only edit the proof body of the original declaration. Preserve the statement, existing imports, and top-level context.
provenance.objective: Compare measured full competition score; source style preferences are not an acceptance policy.
provenance.interaction: One-shot candidate generation. These cards do not grant tools or request further model calls.
provenance.evidence_policy: All card evidence is empty until a separately recorded target-environment experiment measures the particular transformation. No universal tactic heartbeat cost or version guarantee is asserted.
provenance.example_policy: No benchmark proofs, benchmark winners, or external before/after examples are included.
provenance.retrieval_policy: Triggers are simple lexical hints, not evidence that preconditions hold. The harness may select a bounded subset.
adaptation_notes: No copied skill workflows, automatic priorities, risk-free claims, or promised percentage savings.
No edits to declarations, definitions, global attributes, imports, compiler options, or trust boundaries.
Do not introduce sorry, axioms, native_decide, or kernel-bypassing primitives.
A newer upstream recommendation is not proof of availability in the benchmark toolchain.

cards.title: Use an available theorem directly
preconditions: A supplied or already available lemma has the required conclusion.
All arguments and side conditions can be supplied.
cards.action: Replace the derivation by that lemma application; use its exact type to determine argument order.
failure_modes: A remembered name may be absent in the pinned project.
A similar conclusion can hide stronger hypotheses.

cards.title: Remove a redundant tactic wrapper
preconditions: The enclosed term elaborates with the same expected type.
cards.action: Use the term directly in place of a single-step by block.
failure_modes: Removing the tactic context can change elaboration of implicit arguments.

cards.title: Construct the proof directly
preconditions: The subgoal proofs and their dependencies are known.
cards.action: Combine an apply/exact sequence into a lemma application, or constructor branches into an anonymous constructor.
failure_modes: Dependent arguments may require annotations.
Implicit argument order need not match tactic subgoal order.

cards.title: Remove forwarding lambdas
preconditions: A lambda only forwards its bound arguments in order.
cards.action: Replace the forwarding function by the function it calls when their types coincide.
failure_modes: Coercions, dependent types, or instance arguments may require the lambda.

cards.title: Inline a small local proof
preconditions: The fact has one use and its expected type remains recoverable.
cards.action: Substitute the proof term at its use; keep a type annotation if needed.
failure_modes: Context-sensitive tactics may lose useful hypotheses.
Repeated work or difficult inference can increase heartbeats.

cards.title: Remove a redundant local fact
preconditions: No later term, tactic search, or instance synthesis needs the declaration.
cards.action: Delete the unnecessary local declaration or unused classical opening.
failure_modes: Automation may consume a fact without naming it.
Removing classical can alter available decidability instances.

cards.title: Close with a nearby fact
preconditions: A known fact matches the goal after the same simplifications.
cards.action: Use simpa with that fact and the necessary rules; use exact if simplification is unnecessary.
failure_modes: Simplifying a fact differs from simplifying only the goal.
Broad simplification can change across versions.

cards.title: Control the simplifier rule set
preconditions: The needed rules are already known or supplied in context.
cards.action: Consider an explicit only list; remove redundant entries while retaining configuration and location.
failure_modes: A missing rule can leave an open goal.
A longer list can outweigh any heartbeat saving.
Explicit lemma names still require version checks.

cards.title: Reduce arithmetic search inputs
preconditions: Only a subset of the facts is mathematically needed.
cards.action: Supply the relevant arithmetic facts and eliminate redundant hints without changing the intended inequalities.
failure_modes: Nonlinear preprocessing may require auxiliary products or squares.
Removing a fact can make search more expensive.

cards.title: Choose arithmetic automation for the goal
preconditions: The chosen tactic is available in the current imports and pinned versions.
cards.action: Consider omega for Nat/Int linear constraints, ring for polynomial identities, norm_num for numeric normalization, or positivity for structural signs.
failure_modes: Variable multiplication exceeds Presburger arithmetic.
Division and casts need appropriate side conditions.
A short tactic is not necessarily cheap.

cards.title: Transfer a known property across equality
preconditions: A simpler function has the desired property and agrees on the relevant domain.
cards.action: Apply an available congruence or transfer lemma with the equality proof.
failure_modes: Equality direction, domains, and pointwise side conditions matter.
Global equality may be stronger than the available local equality.

cards.title: Use the appropriate extensionality principle
preconditions: The objects have an available extensionality theorem.
cards.action: Reduce equality to the relevant pointwise or field equalities, sharing a common closing argument where possible.
failure_modes: Over-extending can create extra goals.
Dependent fields and coercions can require a more specific theorem.

cards.title: Reuse repeated work inside the proof
preconditions: Several regions repeat the same derivation with compatible parameters.
cards.action: Prove a local fact or local parameterized helper once and reuse it within the unchanged declaration.
failure_modes: Extra parameters and generality can increase elaboration.
Do not add a top-level helper or change the statement.

cards.title: Give elaboration useful type information
preconditions: Nested polymorphic applications or ambiguous coercions obscure the expected type.
cards.action: Use a typed local fact, explicit argument, or type ascription at the ambiguous application.
failure_modes: Extra annotation increases source length.
Overspecified types can reduce version compatibility.

cards.title: Use an explicit proof instead of repeating search
preconditions: A complete explicit replacement is supplied or can be constructed from known facts.
cards.action: Write the explicit term or replay script, preserving all obligations; do not invent a tool result.
failure_modes: A suggested script can require adjustment.
Longer replay code may score worse.
A partial apply suggestion does not close the proof.

cards.title: Shorten an elementary calculation chain
preconditions: Intermediate steps are established and compose in the required direction.
cards.action: Replace a short calc chain by the corresponding transitivity application or composition.
failure_modes: Mixed relations may need a specific transitivity lemma.
The calc block may supply essential expected types.

cards.title: Remove unnecessary rewrite steps
preconditions: A rewrite is redundant for the remainder of the proof.
cards.action: Remove the redundant rule or combine compatible consecutive rewrites, preserving order and location.
failure_modes: A later tactic may depend on the exact normal form.
Changing occurrence selection or rewriting hypotheses changes the state.

cards.title: Use compositional function-property reasoning
preconditions: Required property lemmas or an appropriate imported tactic are available.
cards.action: Replace repetitive property plumbing with a direct compositional lemma application, or a supported specialized tactic.
failure_modes: A tactic may be absent in older versions.
Side conditions can require more work than the original explicit proof.
